note: Adapted from the entry of Chhotani (1997), originally in English; the soldier, the worker and the alate are all available, the worker is dimorphic; synonymy lists, figure numbers and distribution records are not translated. The original entry takes O. gurdaspurensis as its heading, and the first line of the synonymy list is Odontotermes (Cyclotermes) obesus f. gurdaspurensis; the two soldier head-width indices are damaged in the OCR of the original (given as “0.S9” and “0.5S—0.6S”) and are not entered in the text.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule and body dark brown; antennae brown; postclypeus, labrum and legs yellowish brown. Head and body densely setose. Body length with wings 27.0–30.0 mm, without wings 14.0–15.75 mm. Head capsule subcircular (to mandibular base 1.65–2.00 mm, width including the compound eyes 2.45–2.80 mm). Fontanelle minute, circular, raised. Compound eyes subcircular, large (maximum diameter 0.68–0.80 mm, minimum diameter 0.58–0.70 mm); close to the lower margin of the head. Ocelli large, oval (long diameter 0.23–0.30 mm, short diameter 0.15–0.20 mm); separated from the compound eye by about their short diameter (eye–ocellus distance 0.15–0.18 mm). Antennae 19-segmented; segment 3 shortest. Postclypeus inflated, setose; slightly less than half as long as wide. Pronotum nearly trapezoidal (length 1.20–1.40 mm, width 2.25–2.60 mm); with a paler T-shaped median mark and 2 oval shoulder spots; anterior margin slightly raised, wavy and with a shallow median notch; posterior margin weakly to deeply concave. Wings long, setose apically (forewing 23.0–26.0 mm, hindwing 20.6–23.50 mm); the radial band arises at about the apical 1/3; the wing micro-sculpturing consists of papillae and rod-like structures of the obesus type.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule golden yellow to dark brown; antennae yellowish brown, paler at the base; mandibles reddish brown to dark brown; body yellow to pale yellowish brown. Head sparsely setose, body more densely setose. Body length 5.0–6.50 mm. Head capsule subrectangular to oval; the sides nearly parallel, weakly constricted in front of the antennae (to mandibular base 1.42–1.63 mm, maximum width 1.20–1.40 mm, width at the mandibular base 0.73–0.95 mm). Antennae 16-segmented; segment 4 shortest. Labrum wide, lingulate; slightly longer than wide; anterior margin rounded. Mandibles long and slender, weakly incurved (length 0.95–1.08 mm); longer than half the head length (mandible length/head length index 0.63–0.72). Left mandible with 1 conspicuous, sharp tooth situated slightly behind the apical 1/3 (tooth distance 0.33–0.45 mm, tooth distance/mandible length index 0.33–0.40). Right mandible with a small tooth at the middle 1/3 of the mandible. Postmentum subrectangular, the sides weakly convex (length 0.80–1.0 mm, maximum width 0.40–0.55 mm). Pronotum saddle-shaped (length 0.50–0.70 mm, width 0.85–1.0 mm).

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Dimorphic. Major worker: head capsule pale yellow to golden yellow; antennae pale yellow at the base and darker apically; legs and body nearly white. Head and body rather densely setose. Body length 4.5–5.2 mm. Head capsule subquadrate (to mandibular base 1.25–1.40 mm, maximum width 1.45–1.65 mm). Antennae 17-segmented; segments 3 and 5 shortest and about equal in length. Postclypeus inflated and setose; less than half as long as wide. Pronotum saddle-shaped (length 0.40–0.58 mm, width 0.74–0.90 mm); anterior margin deeply concave, posterior margin broadly concave. Minor worker: similar to the major worker but smaller, head capsule subrectangular to oval; body length 3.5–4.0 mm, head length to mandibular base 0.65–0.80 mm, maximum head width 0.95–1.10 mm, pronotal length 0.35–0.48 mm, width 0.55–0.70 mm.
